transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First off, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a full month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel or drops for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're not sure about the specific product you have, I'd recommend checking with your GP or pharmacist to confirm it's okay to use.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the information. Another thing I'm wondering about is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please contact your care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

How long ago was your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It was about a week ago. I'll keep an eye on it. Thank you for all your help. I don't have any more questions.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's good to know. A week is still very early, so some blurriness is normal at this stage, but as I mentioned, it should improve quickly.

Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they have. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and wishing you a smooth recovery.

verdict.label: pass

It also covered `mild_case_advice` with, "If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside." Finally, `escalation_criteria` was addressed by, "However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further."
